places.name: Malaca
past: Planted on the height above the landing: the upper town about its largo, with the Sé and the câmara, and a short grid of streets along the brow; below, the landing’s warehouses and its rua direita along the shore, and steep ladeiras between them.
Walled.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
A great fire burned 33 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 15% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 37 houses were built into what was left of it.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 14 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the southern side; 46 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 13 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.
The Carmelites were given ground by the wall for their friary.
A great fire burned 43 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
